chapters.title: What you are looking at
chapters.narration: This is TENET5 — a public record of Canadian government decisions, built entirely from primary sources: Hansard transcripts, Auditor General reports, Health Canada data, court documents, and sworn testimony. Nothing on this site is opinion. Every claim links to the document that proves it. Over the next twelve minutes, LIRIL will walk you through what the record shows.

chapters.title: Why this record exists
chapters.narration: Accountability systems only work when someone keeps the receipts. This page is the master thesis: what this record is for, how to read it, and the standard every page must meet — a primary government or court document behind every claim. If a source cannot be produced, the claim does not appear.

chapters.title: The pipeline that produces the outcome
chapters.narration: Outcomes are not accidents — they are produced by structure. Six flow charts trace how money, lobbying, appointments and legislation move through the federal system, and where oversight fails at each junction. Follow any chart from left to right and you can see exactly where public interest exits the pipeline.

chapters.title: The numbers Health Canada publishes
chapters.narration: Medical assistance in dying: seventy-six thousand, four hundred and seventy-five deaths recorded since 2016, with sixteen and a half thousand in 2024 alone — four point seven percent of all Canadian deaths. These are Health Canada's own annual reports. The record maps each expansion of eligibility, and each vote that enabled it.

chapters.title: When the state offered death to veterans
chapters.narration: Veterans Affairs caseworkers offered assisted death to veterans who called asking for help — including a Paralympian asking for a wheelchair ramp. These cases are documented in committee testimony and the department's own admissions. The record holds each documented case, and what happened to the people who reported it.

chapters.title: Housing as a produced crisis
chapters.narration: Two hundred and thirty-five thousand or more Canadians experience homelessness in a year, while the housing budget delivered a fraction of what was promised. This page tracks CMHC's own figures against announced spending — forty-four billion announced, three point eight six billion verifiably delivered.

chapters.title: A fertility rate of 1.26
chapters.narration: Statistics Canada records the national fertility rate at one point two six — far below replacement. The record examines the documented policy environment behind it: housing costs, delayed family formation, and a demographic strategy that substitutes imported population for domestic births, adopted without a parliamentary vote.

chapters.title: The oldest chapter of the pattern
chapters.narration: The Truth and Reconciliation Commission documented the residential school system as cultural genocide in 2015. The National Inquiry into Missing and Murdered Indigenous Women reached a genocide finding in 2019. These are Canada's own official findings — the legal anchor for everything this record measures against.

chapters.title: Where the money actually goes
chapters.narration: ArriveCAN: a two-hundred-and-thirty-eight-times cost overrun. Phoenix pay: nine point three billion dollars to break payroll. McKinsey sole-source contracts. One hundred and three billion dollars in documented government failure, traced through the Auditor General's own findings and the public accounts.

chapters.title: Who decides Canadian policy
chapters.narration: The Hogue Commission and NSICOP documented foreign interference in Canadian elections and named the People's Republic of China as the principal state actor. Intelligence showed parliamentarians working on behalf of foreign states. The record maps the documented networks — states, lobbies, media ownership — and the enforcement that never came.

chapters.title: The pipeline year by year — and where it points
chapters.narration: Placed on a single timeline, the pattern is visible: each documented expansion follows the last. MAID eligibility for mental illness alone is already scheduled in law for March 2027. The Century Initiative's one-hundred-million-population target remains the adopted planning assumption. Digital identity infrastructure continues to build on the ArriveCAN precedent. The record does not speculate — it shows you the scheduled next steps the documents already contain.

chapters.title: Named, sourced, citizen-actionable
chapters.narration: Every documented ethics violation, criminal charge, conviction and scandal involving Canadian elected officials — federal and provincial — in one database. One thousand one hundred and five confirmed records. Each entry cites its source. This is the verdict layer of the record: not allegations — documentation.

chapters.title: What one citizen can actually do
chapters.narration: The record exists so that citizens can act on it. Section 504 of the Criminal Code lets any person lay an information before a justice. This page holds the filing guide, the petitions, the letters, and the press kit. Share one page. File one complaint. The record is permanent — and it is yours. This concludes the documentary. Explore any chapter at your own pace.
